titulo: Three ways an agent can use your site: read, operate the screen, call a tool
titulo_curto: Three ways to use a site
lead: When an AI agent reaches your site, it does one of three things: it reads the HTML, it operates the screen like a person, or it calls a tool the site has declared. In this lesson you run all three against a sample page and against a real site, and see which one works in each case.
objetivo: tell reading, operating the screen, and calling a tool apart, and see all three running against the kit's sample page.

aprende.t: Read: what a fetch pulls out of your HTML
Operate the screen: the agent finds each field by name
Call a tool: MCP on the server, WebMCP on the page
The course kit running on your machine

hero_alt: The back of a dark monitor with three cables of different thicknesses reaching different connectors.

secoes.titulo: One request, three paths to your site

nos.detalhe: Search and fetch tools download the page and pull out the text. Many don't run JavaScript: what isn't in the HTML doesn't exist for them. Showing up in AI answers is a topic for the inemaSEO Program.

A browser agent opens the page, finds the controls, and clicks, types, and chooses. Playwright MCP hands the model the page's accessibility tree instead of a screenshot (lesson 2). Finding the field depends on the name the HTML gives it.

The site declares a function with a name, a description, and input as JSON Schema, and the agent calls it. On the server this is MCP, stable (revision 2026-07-28). On the page it is WebMCP, a Community Group draft from 10/16/2026 that only runs with an origin trial or a flag (lessons 4 and 5).
All three coexist. Today almost every agent reads or operates the screen; few browsers expose WebMCP. That's why well-made HTML comes before any tool, and a tool never replaces the form.

secoes.legenda: Agents that call tools are still a minority in Oct 2026; agents that read and agents that operate the screen show up every day.

secoes.sub: Request: "schedule a full service for Ana on 10/25".

texto: The agent downloads the HTML and finds out there's a form with three labels. It knows what the page offers, but it doesn't schedule anything: reading doesn't submit.
If the form only appears after JavaScript runs, a reader without a browser never even learns it exists.
The agent opens the page, finds the "Seu nome" field, the "Serviço" field, the "Data" field and the "Agendar" button, and clicks. It works if every control has a name.
On the kit's old page, the name is only in the placeholder and the button is a div: the agent gets stuck on the first field.

exemplo.texto: An agent looks things up by role and name ("text field Seu nome", "button Agendar"). A placeholder disappears when the person types, and a div is not a button to anyone reading the accessibility tree.

texto: If the page registered a scheduling tool, the agent would pass name, service and date as JSON and get the response back, without clicking anything.
In the kit's Chromium the API doesn't exist: the example page has no origin trial token. inema.club does, and there the same Chromium lists the tools.

secoes.sub: Just once. It clones the course repository into ~/projetos, installs Playwright 1.63.0 (pinned version, from 09/04/2026) and downloads its Chromium. No step in the course calls a model.

blocos.conteudo:
[ -d ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72 ] || git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/formacao-webmcp-base-v72 ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72/kit
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npx playwright install chromium
node -e "import('playwright').then(p => console.log('playwright pronto:', p.chromium.executablePath().split('/').slice(-3).join('/')))"

abas.html:
added 2 packages in 210ms
playwright pronto: chromium-1243/chrome-linux-arm64/chrome

The first time, npx playwright install chromium downloads the browser (a few hundred MB). The last line shows the Chromium folder the kit will use; on Mac and x86 Linux the name changes.

secoes.titulo: The three ways against the example page
secoes.sub: The kit serves the Oficina Pedal Livre (a fictional bike shop) page on a server of your own, at 127.0.0.1, and runs the three ways. depois.html has semantic HTML; antes.html is the same screen without labels.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72/kit
for p in depois antes; do echo "## $p.html"; node tres-jeitos.mjs $p; echo "saída: $?"; done

abas.html:
## depois.html
1 · ler     2.2 KB de HTML · h1: Agendar revisão · <form>: 1 · <label>: 3
2 · operar  achou 3 campos e o botão pelo nome · tela diz: Pedido recebido (simulação): revisão completa em 2026-10-25, Ana
3 · chamar  document.modelContext: ausente neste Chromium 153.0.8010.12 → sem ferramentas declaradas, o agente fica no jeito 2
saída: 0
## antes.html
1 · ler     1.7 KB de HTML · h1: (sem <h1>) · <form>: 0 · <label>: 0
2 · operar  travou: não achou o campo "Seu nome" pelo nome em 2 s (o agente teria de adivinhar pela tela)
3 · chamar  document.modelContext: ausente neste Chromium 153.0.8010.12 → sem ferramentas declaradas, o agente fica no jeito 2
saída: 1

Same screen, opposite result. In depois.html the agent schedules; in antes.html it can't even find the first field, and the script exits with 1. Way 3 is absent in both: the example page has no origin trial token.

The screenshot of antes.html and the one of depois.html are almost the same: same text, same yellow button. Anyone who tests only by looking thinks it's done. The test that counts is the agent's: find each control by role and name. Lesson 2 shows what it receives and lesson 3 fixes it.

secoes.titulo: The three ways on a real site
secoes.sub: The same script against inema.club, which belongs to INEMA. In your case, use only your own site: the script reads and lists, and never clicks or runs a tool outside the kit.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72/kit
node tres-jeitos.mjs https://<your-site>/<page with a form>; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
1 · ler     104.2 KB de HTML · h1: INEMA.CLUB Portal INEMA · <form>: 1 · <label>: 1
2 · operar  146 controles na árvore · 0 sem nome (esses o agente teria de adivinhar pela tela)
3 · chamar  document.modelContext: presente neste Chromium 153.0.8010.12 · 8 ferramenta(s) registrada(s): buscar_conhecimento, buscar_cursos, comparar_cursos, consultar_atualizacoes, …
saída: 0

On the real site, way 2 counts the controls in the tree and how many have no name. Way 3 shows up: inema.club publishes an origin trial token in a meta tag, and the kit's Chromium 153 (inside the trial's 149–156 range) exposes document.modelContext. The script only calls getTools(), which lists; it doesn't run any tool.

secoes.sub: The concept in 30 s. Two notes from 10/19/2026: the "form that becomes a tool" is the declarative API, which was left out of the spec and only exists in Chrome; and security doesn't rest on the site alone: prompt injection has no solution, and course 4 covers it.
Kit installed, the three ways on the example page and on your site.

exercicios.texto: Run the "install" block. If you already have the repository in ~/projetos, it only installs the dependencies.
exercicios.pronto: the block ends with the line playwright pronto: followed by the Chromium folder (e.g. chromium-1243/…/chrome).

exercicios.texto: Run the "after and before" block and compare line 2 of the two pages.
exercicios.pronto: node tres-jeitos.mjs depois → 2 · operar achou 3 campos e o botão pelo nome and saída: 0; node tres-jeitos.mjs antes → travou and saída: 1.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Your site, the three ways
exercicios.texto: Run the template on the page of your site that has the most important form (contact, booking, search). Write down the three lines: they go into the plan for lesson 8.
exercicios.pronto: the output has the lines 1 · ler, 2 · operar and 3 · chamar, and ends with saída: 0 (no unnamed controls) or saída: 1 with the number of unnamed controls noted down.

perguntas.p: An agent downloads the HTML of your booking page and replies that a form exists. Which of the three ways did it use?
opcoes: Calling a tool, because it found the form
Reading: it pulled the information from the HTML, without sending anything
Operating the screen, because it saw the form
None: without WebMCP the agent doesn't understand forms
perguntas.explica: Reading is downloading and extracting. It knows the form exists, but it doesn't book anything. Operating would require opening the page and clicking; calling would require a declared tool.

perguntas.p: antes.html and depois.html look the same on screen. Why does the agent get stuck only on antes.html?
opcoes: Because antes.html is heavier and takes longer to load
Because antes.html has no origin trial token
Because the fields have no name and the button is a div
Because the kit's Chromium refuses pages without lang
perguntas.explica: The agent looks for each control by role and name. Without a label and without a button, there is nothing to look for. The origin trial token only changes way 3, which is absent from both pages.

perguntas.p: On inema.club, way 3 shows up with 8 tools; on the kit's page, it doesn't. What explains the difference in the same Chromium 153?
opcoes: inema.club has an origin trial token; the kit doesn't
inema.club uses an MCP server instead of the page's HTML
WebMCP became a standard and only the kit's page is out of date
The kit's script runs the tools from inema.club
perguntas.explica: WebMCP is a draft (10/16/2026) and Chrome only exposes the API with an origin trial token (149 to 156) or a local flag. The script only lists with getTools(), it doesn't run anything.

perguntas.p: Where do you start preparing a site for agents in Oct/2026?
opcoes: Register WebMCP tools and take the form off the page
Create an llms.txt before anything else on the site
Wait for WebMCP to become a standard so you don't redo the work
HTML with the right names, to read and operate today
perguntas.explica: Almost every agent reads or operates the screen today. The tool comes later and never replaces the form, which is the path for anyone without the API.

itens.texto: Read the HTML, operate the screen, call a declared tool.
To operate the screen, the agent finds each control by role and name.
WebMCP only shows up with an origin trial; the form is still the path.
